P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: No surrender or conversion requirement was found. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act mainly regulates outflows: from July 2023, individuals can remit up to USD 100,000 a year abroad without documentation, up from USD 50,000. Banks may ask the reason for large inbound receipts. Rules specific to freelancers' inbound service income were not captured.
P1_fx_receipts.note: Single secondary source (Korea Times, 2023 announcement) captured on 2026-10-22; FETA/enforcement decree not captured.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Korean banks offer foreign-currency deposit accounts (외화예금), split by residence into resident accounts (거주자계정), external accounts (대외계정) and emigrant accounts. TRAP for foreign residents: foreigners cannot open the resident account (except foreign residents running a business in Korea for a business account) and use the external account instead (KB Think).

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: A sole proprietor (개인사업자) registers with the National Tax Service via Hometax or a local tax office within 20 days of the business start date. There is no government fee and no minimum capital. Foreign nationals need a visa that permits the activity (e.g. F-2, F-4, F-5, F-6, D-8) and an Alien Registration Card. The NTS does not check visa status at registration, but operating outside the visa's scope is an immigration violation. Online sellers must also file a mail-order business report (통신판매업 신고, not captured).

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents are individuals domiciled in Korea or residing there 183+ days in a tax year; from 2026 this also covers 183 consecutive days spanning two tax years. Residents are taxed on worldwide income, but foreign residents with five years or less in the last ten are taxed on foreign-source income only if it is paid in or remitted to Korea. Rates are 6%–45% plus local income tax of 10% of the national tax. Freelancers' business income is commonly subject to 3.3% withholding (3% + 0.3%) as a prepayment, settled in the May comprehensive income tax return.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 10%, and every registered business is in the VAT system. There is no general exemption threshold, but sole proprietors with prior-year sales under ₩104 million (since July 2024) can use the simplified-taxpayer regime; under ₩48 million they pay no VAT but still file. Zero rating applies to exports of goods and to certain listed services to non-residents or foreign corporations where payment is received in foreign currency. For some services this applies only on a reciprocal basis.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA), enforced by the PIPC, applies to all personal data controllers. An amendment of 10 March 2026, with most provisions effective 11 September 2026, raised the maximum administrative penalty from 3% to 10% of total revenue for repeated wilful or grossly negligent violations or failure to follow PIPC corrective orders, and names the business owner as ultimately responsible.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Under Article 17 of the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, buyers can withdraw from an online purchase for any reason within 7 days of receiving the goods, regardless of the seller's policy, subject to statutory exceptions. Opening the package to inspect does not forfeit the right. If goods don't match the description, the window extends to 3 months from delivery or 30 days from discovery, and the seller pays return shipping. Digital subscriptions can be cancelled within 7 days for unused content.
L6_consumer_ecommerce.note: Single secondary domain (Seoulstart) captured; law.go.kr English page captured without body text on 2026-10-22.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving). Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
